High-rise office tower.provides: long travel distances, stair capacity limits, refuge floors, fire-resisting compartments

Underground metro station.provides: single direction of egress, no external windows, rapid smoke logging

Single-storey warehouse.provides: short escape distances, many exits, large undivided volume

Hospital ward.requires: movement of people who cannot self-evacuate
Hospital ward.provides: fire compartments designed for transfer, staff trained to move patients, beds and equipment

Able-bodied staff familiar with the buil.provides: fast self-evacuation, knowledge of secondary exits, capacity to assist

Members of the public unfamiliar with ex.provides: slow response, tendency to return to the entrance used, no knowledge of alternatives

Non-ambulatory patients.provides: no self-evacuation whatsoever, dependence on staff ratio and equipment

Night shift skeleton crew.provides: very fast self-evacuation, almost no capacity to assist anyone else

Simultaneous total evacuation.requires: escape capacity sufficient for everyone at once
Simultaneous total evacuation.provides: everyone out fastest, overwhelms stairs in tall buildings

Phased floor-by-floor.requires: compartments that hold long enough to wait, and a public address system
Phased floor-by-floor.provides: controlled stair loading, requires occupants to accept waiting

Defend in place.requires: fire-resisting construction and confidence in it
Defend in place.provides: no movement of occupants, total dependence on compartment integrity

Horizontal transfer to an adjacent compa.requires: at least two compartments on the same level
Horizontal transfer to an adjacent compa.provides: movement without stairs, suitable for people who cannot descend

Dense smoke in escape routes.requires: fire products entering the means of escape

Loss of lighting.requires: failure of normal and emergency supply
Loss of lighting.provides: disorientation, no effect on physical route capacity

Blocked primary exit.requires: an obstruction or fire at one route
Blocked primary exit.provides: loss of one path, capacity of the remainder unchanged

Lift systems unavailable.provides: no vertical mechanical transport, irrelevant where escape is horizontal

_v1_notes.BUILDING TYPE|OCCUPANT PROFILE: non-ambulatory patients are N outside a hospital ward - an office tower, a metro station and a warehouse do not hold people who cannot self-evacuate as a population. A night skeleton crew is N in a metro station, which is either open to the public or closed.
_v1_notes.BUILDING TYPE|EVACUATION STRATEGY: a metro station and a warehouse both have a single-level escape with no second compartment, so phased, defend-in-place and horizontal transfer are all N. A hospital ward is N for simultaneous total evacuation: moving every non-ambulatory patient at once is not achievable.
_v1_notes.BUILDING TYPE|IMPAIRMENT: lifts unavailable is N in a metro station and a warehouse, where escape is not by lift.
_v1_notes.OCCUPANT PROFILE|EVACUATION STRATEGY: the unfamiliar public will not accept phased waiting and cannot be relied on to defend in place, so both N. Non-ambulatory patients cannot do simultaneous or phased stair evacuation at all. A skeleton crew is N for defend in place, having no capacity to manage it.
_v1_notes.EVACUATION STRATEGY|IMPAIRMENT: phased evacuation and defend in place are both N with dense smoke in escape routes - both depend on the escape route or compartment holding, which smoke ingress has already disproved.
